concepts.label: Cluster backup (Cloud Snapshot)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - first appearance of the backup: namespace this batch; the whole-cluster, storage-level backup mechanism distinct from a per-bucket backup

relations.subject: capella:maintenance-job
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - a recommended, not enforced, sequencing precondition; still the same ordering-precondition shape as the Cost-Based Optimizer/UPDATE STATISTICS case this predicate was first minted for
relations.evidence: Before upgrading your operational cluster with a patch, minor, or major release version, [back up your entire production cluster](#backup-cluster) and [review SDK compatibility](#sdk-compatibility).

relations.subject: capella:maintenance-job
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - recommended precondition for minor/major upgrades specifically
relations.evidence: For minor and major cluster upgrades, [test your application](#test-application) in a controlled staging environment.

relations.subject: capella:staging-cluster
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - one of two documented ways to seed a staging cluster with production data
relations.evidence: Use the `cbbackupmgr` CLI tool to back up and restore data at the bucket level. This method does not restore a full cluster backup from your production cluster to your staging cluster. You must back up each individual bucket from your production cluster and restore them into pre-created buckets on your staging cluster.

relations.subject: capella:staging-cluster
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - the alternative, full-cluster-backup method of seeding a staging cluster
relations.evidence: Restore a full cluster backup to your new staging cluster. For more information, see [Restore a Cluster Backup](restore-cloud-snapshot.md).

relations.subject: capella:staging-cluster
relations.evidence: If you need your staging cluster to stay in sync with your production cluster, create a [one way XDCR replication](#clusters:xdcr:manage-xdcr-replications.adoc) to migrate your data between the clusters.

notable_absence.finding: No capella-role:* gate appears on this page at all - every action described (backing up, testing, creating a staging cluster) is framed as a recommended best practice, not a role-gated procedure (those gates live on the pages this one links to, e.g. take-cloud-snapshot.md's Project Owner prerequisite). Also zero AWS/Azure/GCP-specific content - upgrade best practices are presented as CSP-uniform, consistent with upgrade-database.json's same finding.

cross_component_finding: This page is the connective tissue between two otherwise-separate parts of this batch: it explicitly recommends backup/restore (cloud-snapshots.md and cli-backup-restore.md) as pre-upgrade insurance ('Backups are a good security measure, minimizing the risk associated with the upgrade process. In a disaster recovery scenario, you'd have the option to restore your cluster backup and have backwards compatibility with the cluster versioning.'), tying the backup/restore surface and the upgrade surface together as a single risk-management workflow rather than two independent features.
cross_product_finding: The 'community-supported only' wording in this page's NOTE ('For clusters that are community-supported only, use the Couchbase forums, Discord channel and documentation... for support and feedback') is a new, third support-tier phrasing distinct from both the plan:* support-plan family (Enterprise/Developer Pro/Basic/Free Tier Support Plan) and from server/'s Enterprise/Community Edition axis - it describes a lack of a paid support channel, not an edition or a named plan tier. Flagging as a possible fourth wording variant for the already-known support-plan wording inconsistency, not resolved here.
